findings.reason: the decision text asserts a reuse that did not happen, so the plan must either extend `review.py` to a key-aware store or state why the plan-review key (version+blob fingerprint) cannot share it.
findings.text: `plan_review_path`/`store_plan_review`/`read_plan_review` re-implement the legacy-path-plus-`.at-<blob>`-sibling keying, the predecessor-preserving target choice and the newest-record read that `reckon/crew/review.py` already owns (`review_path`, `_partial_review_path`, `store_review`, `read_review`), sharing only `review_store_root`; the plan's locked decision (review-store) states it "reuses the code-review machinery," which the code does only at the store root

findings.reason: the plan should name `resources.resolve_resource` as the owner of plan resolution and have the sweep and the gate resolve one file the same way.
findings.text: `plan_review_subject` builds its plan path as `docs / "plans" / f"{slug}.html"` behind its own slug regex and `is_file()` check, bypassing `reckon/resources.py:resolve_resource`, the typed resolver that the sibling gate in the same feature uses (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2671`); the sweep's notion of "the plan" can therefore diverge from the gate's on archived, duplicated or non-canonically-placed plans

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` hides fingerprinting, the record shape, the store join and report delivery behind a small function set, and the dispatch composer and the sweep extend their owners in `reckon/crew/recovery.py` rather than spreading new shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan-review store re-implements the review store's path/read convention rather than extending it, and the review subject re-implements plan path resolution rather than extending `resolve_resource`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the code-review store as its record home (decision review-store), the existing review reflex it extends (D6), the review-role exemption predicate `_is_review_node`, and `reckon/interface_counts.py` for its budget; my search of `reckon/` confirms each exists and is reused (`reckon/crew/review.py:979 review_store_root`, `reckon/crew/recovery.py:238`, `reckon/crew/recovery.py:4121` sweep block, `reckon/interface_counts.py:38`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan-review dispatch extends the code-review composer (`_review_dispatch_fields`, `reckon/crew/recovery.py:490`, handles both subjects in one function) and the gate extends the dispatch guard; no unjustified parallel layer was found beyond the store and resolver forks reported below.
